newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Gilts to struggle at 114-24 barrier.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Gilts to struggle at 114-24 barrier.

text.p: June gilt futures on LIFFE will have a difficult time overcoming the top at recent highs around 114-24 on Thursday and will likely head for the 114-13 area initially, technical analysts said.

"We're going to continue to see resistance from the recent highs at 114-20 and 114-24," Anne Whitby, head of technical analysis at 4CAST in London, said. "Obviously those would have to be cleared to target higher levels."
Gilts were down 2/32 at 114-15, just after the open at 0700 GMT. On Wednesday, they hit a 114-20 high but could not surmount Tuesday's 114-23 high and the 114-24 contract high hit on May 9.
On a downward move, gilts would first head for the 114-14 area on Thursday, a congestion and buying area from Wednesday, Whitby said.
"If that breaks the next target is at 114-05, which was quite a strong buying level from yesterday. We had a good bounce up from there," she said.
"That should attract some buyers again but there is a risk during the day of testing the lows at 114-00 and 113-29," Whitby added.
Gilts hit a 114-03 low on Wednesday and a 113-29 low on May 12. On May 9 it hit a 113-30 low.
Whitby said if gilts did manage to bash through 114-24 they would head for an extenstion target at 115-05.
Richard Adcock, manager of technical research at HSBC Futures in London, also expected gilts to stall with evidence growing upside momentum is slowing against overbought readings.

"Stochastics are now beginning to roll over against this overextended position and while these have not yet given a sell signal, it is looking increasingly likely that consolidation will develop," he said in a note.
He looked for pullbacks to the 113-00 area over the next few days.
September short sterling futures were quoted at 93.24, down 0.01 from Wednesday.

Tom Hobson, director of technical analysis at Merrill Lynch in London, said the rally in UK fixed income markets has come to a halt, noting March 1998 short sterling was capped now by recent resistance.
He said the market had gone into the May British election undervalued but after strong gains it was now overvalued.
March 1998 short sterling last week topped out at 93.07, a resistance area which coincided with highs in mid-March. At 0720 GMT it was at 93.97, down 0.01.
